Analysts point to the Lions' roster depth and home edge, with betting lines favoring them by 7 points against the Saints' young QB Tyler Shough and new schemes from coach Kellen Moore. Ingraham mocked him for faking football fandom, but supporters pointed to his student-era posts, a 2016 crowd-surfing photo at a game, and his self-described diehard loyalty as a UT alum. The exchange highlighted how Texas college sports stir deep state pride amid Talarico's tight race against Ken Paxton, with even the Longhorns account joining the hook 'em cheers.

data.hook: With under 20 seconds left, Brandon High Jr. broke free for a 25-yard touchdown run, capping Owen McCown's clutch final drive and sending Roadrunners fans into celebration.
data.name: UTSA Roadrunners Rally for 100th Win, Reclaim I-35 Rivalry Over Texas State
data.summary: The UTSA Roadrunners came from behind to beat rival Texas State 31-26 on Saturday in San Marcos, securing their 100th program win and taking back the I-35 rivalry trophy. Quarterback Owen McCown converted two fourth downs on the game-winning drive, setting up High's decisive score at Jim Wacker Field. The victory improved UTSA to 2-0, with the team playfully telling the Bobcats to 'PAC that L' while fans hailed the milestone road triumph.

data.hook: Cam Coleman seemed to snag the deep ball over his shoulder, but it popped loose on impact—right into Jaylen McClain's waiting hands for a wild Ohio State pick.
data.name: Jaylen McClain's Fluky Interception Stuns Texas in Ohio State Clash
data.summary: In the first quarter of the top-ranked Buckeyes' primetime matchup against Texas in Austin, quarterback Arch Manning targeted wide-open receiver Cam Coleman on a deep route. Coleman hauled it in mid-air but lost control hitting the turf, allowing Ohio State safety Jaylen McClain to scoop the live ball at the Buckeyes' 19-yard line. The turnover followed Texas' earlier fumble and preserved Ohio State's 3-0 lead after a field goal, capping a rough start for the home team's offense amid a packed stadium.

data.summary: The Buffalo Bills open their 2026 campaign on the road against the Houston Texans on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET from Reliant Stadium, airing on CBS and Paramount+. Buffalo's offense, boosted by new coach Joe Brady, D.J. Moore, and defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard, takes on Houston's stout unit led by C.J. While ESPN and CBS analysts pick a narrow Texans win, public betting leans Bills, setting up a high-stakes quarterback duel for two Super Bowl hopefuls.

data.name: Ohio State Jumps Ahead of Texas in Scorching 163-Degree Showdown
data.summary: No. 1 Ohio State grabbed an early lead over No. 4 Texas in Austin's Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium, where pre-kickoff field temperatures reached 163.6 degrees amid 97-100 degree air. Texas QB Arch Manning's deep shot to wideout Cam Coleman deflected off for a wild interception, sparking debate over whether receiver drops should count as QB stats, as former NFL QB Robert Griffin III noted. Ohio State's opportunistic defense cashed in for a 10-3 edge by the second quarter, boosted by WR Jeremiah Smith's explosive plays.

data.hook: During the 49ers' season opener in Australia, fans flooded timelines with highlights of Daejon Love—a wide receiver who never existed—complete with injury reports and betting props.
data.name: Fake 49ers Player Daejon Love Becomes NFL Meme Sensation
data.summary: Daejon Love, a 35-year-old California man arrested in late August for federal wire fraud, allegedly posed as a 49ers player to scam 26 women out of $1.3 million in fake romance schemes. Social media turned the story into a fictional NFL saga, with memes of Love leading the team tunnel walk, getting carted off injured, and even NBA star Tyrese Haliburton wearing a custom jersey joking he's on IR. The 49ers coach and players joined the fun, while the real team beat the Rams 27-7 amid the online buzz.

data.name: No. 1 Ohio State Faces No. 4 Texas in Austin Tonight
data.summary: ESPN's College GameDay broadcast from the University of Texas campus ahead of the 7:30 p.m. ET kickoff at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium, with both undefeated teams coming off blowout Week 1 wins—Ohio State 56-3 over Ball State and Texas 59-7 over Texas State. Fans fired up the rivalry with playful jabs like a sign mocking Ohio State coach Ryan Day for putting ketchup on brisket, a nod to Texas barbecue pride that even GameDay called out as 'No, just no.' Texas coach Steve Sarkisian kept it simple: 'We're talking about a hell of a football game that's gonna get played tonight.' The Longhorns are slight 1.5-point home favorites, airing on ABC.

data.name: Texas Fans Mock Ryan Day with Ketchup-on-Brisket Signs at GameDay
data.summary: The oversized props targeted Day ahead of the top-five showdown between Texas and Ohio State, turning brisket traditions into fan trash talk during ESPN's College GameDay broadcast. In Texas, where properly smoked brisket reigns supreme, ketchup has no place, making the signs a pointed regional jab that drew laughs, mock outrage, and comeback barbs online. With both teams ranked high and history on the line, the stunt amplified pregame hype in Austin.
